turns.user: Which Midwest hubs are most exposed to winter disruption?

answer.answer:
Of the 7 Midwest hubs, Minneapolis is the most exposed to winter disruption by a wide margin: winter sub-score 75.9, with 34.6 observed winter-disruption days/yr (rank 1 in the portfolio on observed days; rule = snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C) and FEMA NRI winter weather 47.7 / ice storm 32.0.

Next are Detroit (43.5; 10.4 days/yr, portfolio rank 5 on observed days, but the strongest NRI winter inputs in the group at WNTW 77.1 / ISTM 50.4) and Chicago (35.9; 11.8 days/yr, rank 4 observed; WNTW 44.0 / ISTM 33.3). The remaining four cluster tightly: Kansas City 30.5 (8.2 days/yr), Indianapolis 27.7 (7.0), St. Louis 26.7 (5.2) and Columbus 26.3 (6.2 days/yr, tied on observed days with Newark).

For resilience prioritisation, Minneapolis is the clear winter case; Detroit and Chicago are secondary. Note that winter is only one input to the composite — Minneapolis's composite is 36.2 (Moderate), while St. Louis (31.4) and Kansas City (30.7) score Moderate mainly on flood and severe storm.
reasoning: Ranked all 7 Midwest hubs by the winter hazard sub-score.
Minneapolis leads on both observed frequency (34.6 disruption days/yr) and a solid NRI winter component, giving 75.9.
Detroit ranks 2nd on score despite fewer observed days (10.4) because its FEMA NRI winter-weather and ice-storm components are high (77.1 / 50.4).
Chicago has slightly more observed days (11.8) than Detroit but lower NRI components, so it scores 35.9.
Bottom four are closely grouped (26.3-30.5), so differences there are not decision-relevant.
assumptions: Scope limited to the 7 Midwest hubs; scores are 0-100 and relative to this 22-hub portfolio, not absolute probabilities.
Observed days come from point-location daily reanalysis history at each hub, not county-wide conditions.
answer.confidence_reason: Ranking comes directly from the deterministic scoring engine, though the closely grouped lower four make their ordering less meaningful.

Ranking by winter sub-score: Memphis 18.0 (2.0 disruption days/yr, portfolio rank 14; NRI WNTW 31.5 / ISTM 41.1), Charlotte 17.4 (0.4 days/yr, tied on observed days with Atlanta and Houston; ISTM 52.3), Dallas 15.3 (1.2 days/yr), Atlanta 14.6 (0.4), Houston 13.8 (0.4), New Orleans 11.6 (0.2 days/yr) and Miami 0.0 (0.0 days/yr, tied with Los Angeles and Phoenix; NRI winter weather 0.0).

The practical read: no Southern hub warrants winter-specific resilience investment relative to the Midwest. What drives their composites is elsewhere — New Orleans 46.7 (High; hurricane 90.5, flood 81.5), Houston 41.2 (High; flood 92.8, hurricane 72.0), Dallas 35.9 (Moderate; flood 69.3, severe storm 64.9) and Miami 35.4 (Moderate; hurricane 92.7). Memphis, Charlotte and Atlanta all sit in the Low tier.

turns.user: Why is the top one there so exposed?

answer.answer:
Worth flagging the premise: Memphis isn't especially exposed to winter. Its winter sub-score is 18.0 — the highest of the 7 South hubs, but low in portfolio terms (Minneapolis is 75.9), and Memphis's overall composite is 27.0, rank 13 of 22, in the Low tier.

What little winter score it has comes mostly from the FEMA NRI side rather than observed weather: the long-term component is 36.3 (winter weather WNTW 31.5, ice storm ISTM 41.1, weighted 0.4), while observed frequency is just 2.0 winter-disruption days/yr over 2021-2025 (snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C), normalising to only 5.8 and weighted 0.6. Winter contributes 4.5 points of the 27.0 composite. Federal major-disaster declarations since 2000 back this up as occasional rather than chronic: 2 Winter Storm and 2 Severe Ice Storm, against 14 Severe Storm.

What actually drives Memphis is flood and severe storm. Flood scores 51.8 (2.4 heavy-rain days/yr at >= 50 mm, portfolio rank 5, tied with Los Angeles; NRI IFLD 40.3) and contributes 10.4 points. Severe storm scores 38.3 — NRI tornado component 87.7, hail 3.8, severe wind 29.1 — contributing 7.7 points. If you're prioritising Memphis for resilience spend, the case is rainfall/flooding and tornado exposure, not ice and snow.
reasoning: Resolved 'the top one there' as Memphis, highest winter sub-score among the South hubs.
Corrected the premise: 18.0 winter and a 27.0 composite (rank 13/22, Low tier) don't support 'so exposed'.
Decomposed the winter score: observed frequency normalises to 5.8 (weight 0.6) versus NRI long-term 36.3 (weight 0.4), so the NRI ice-storm/winter-weather components carry it.
Winter contributes only 4.5 of the 27.0 composite; flood (10.4) and severe storm (7.7) are the listed top drivers.
Used DR declaration counts as supporting evidence that winter events are episodic there.
assumptions: Scores are 0-100 and relative to this 22-hub portfolio; tiers are prioritisation bands, not probabilities.
Observed day counts cover 2021-2025 only and come from point-location daily history, not county-wide conditions.
Declaration counts are federal major-disaster (DR) declarations since 2000, supporting evidence only.
answer.confidence_reason: The breakdown is deterministic, though a 5-year observation window makes rare Southern winter events noisy.
